items.title: Joe Ascione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: I didn’t see those days of like the Bucky Pizzarellis, the Milt Hintons, the Russell Georges, the Derek Smiths.

ctx.x: Yeah I would think so. I think it’s (a) always been hard, but I don’t think too much has changed in the sense that for example I didn’t see those days of like the Bucky Pizzarellis, the Milt Hintons, the Russell Georges, the Derek Smiths. These guys did five,

ten studio dates a day for years. I’ve done one, like in the last two — I did a Barbie doll commercial. My point is, so in that sense I could say, or if you interviewed them and spoke with them twenty, thirty years ago, has it changed for young guys coming up? Yes and no. I never saw those days so maybe kids today won’t see what I’m seeing. Like let’s say the jazz party scene or jazz festival scene dried up and there’s something else. And they would say oh yeah, guys used to do that, and they did a dozen, two…
